blocks.md: A JOIN connects two tables on a common column. Think Venn diagrams: INNER = intersection, LEFT = left circle + overlap, FULL = both circles.
Every row in employees has a dept_id pointing to departments. JOIN follows that pointer to bring department info into the employee row. It's like looking up a phone number in a directory.

items: Primary key (PK) = unique identifier in parent table (departments.id)
Foreign key (FK) = pointer in child table (employees.dept_id)

sections.title: Inner & Left Joins — The Core Two

blocks.label: inner join
blocks.code:
-- Explicit syntax (preferred)
SELECT e.name, d.name AS department
FROM employees e
INNER JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;

-- Implicit (old style, avoid)
SELECT e.name, d.name
FROM employees e, departments d
WHERE e.dept_id = d.id;
blocks.py-pandas:
# Inner join (default)
merged = employees.merge(departments, left_on='dept_id', right_on='id', how='inner')

# Suffixes for overlapping columns
merged = employees.merge(departments, left_on='dept_id', right_on='id', 
                         how='inner', suffixes=('_emp', '_dept'))
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Explicit join
session.query(Employee.name, Department.name.label('department'))
    .join(Department, Employee.dept_id == Department.id).all()

blocks.label: left join
blocks.code:
-- All employees, even those without department
SELECT e.name, d.name AS department
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;
-- Employees with no dept: d.name = NULL

-- Find employees WITHOUT department
SELECT e.name
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id
WHERE d.id IS NULL;
blocks.py-pandas:
# Left join
merged = employees.merge(departments, left_on='dept_id', right_on='id', how='left')

# Find NULLs (no match)
no_dept = merged[merged['name_dept'].isna()]['name_emp']
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Left join
session.query(Employee.name, Department.name.label('department'))
    .outerjoin(Department, Employee.dept_id == Department.id).all()

# No match
session.query(Employee.name).outerjoin(Department)
    .filter(Department.id.is_(None)).all()

items.q: LEFT JOIN with 10 left rows, 3 matches → result rows:
items.explain: LEFT JOIN returns all left rows (10). 3 matched, 7 NULL-extended.

items.q: WHERE d.id IS NULL after LEFT JOIN finds:
items.explain: NULL-extended rows = no match in right table. Classic anti-join pattern.

blocks.label: right join
blocks.code:
-- All departments, even those with no employees
SELECT d.name, e.name AS employee
FROM employees e
RIGHT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;
-- Departments with no employees: e.name = NULL
blocks.py-pandas:
# Right join
merged = employees.merge(departments, left_on='dept_id', right_on='id', how='right')
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Right join
session.query(Department.name, Employee.name)
    .join(Employee, Department.id == Employee.dept_id, isouter=True).all()

blocks.label: full join
blocks.code:
-- All employees AND all departments
SELECT e.name, d.name
FROM employees e
FULL JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;
-- Matched rows + NULL-extended left + NULL-extended right
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL: no FULL JOIN
-- Workaround: LEFT UNION RIGHT
SELECT * FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON ...
UNION
SELECT * FROM employees e RIGHT JOIN departments d ON ...;
blocks.py-pandas:
# Full outer join
merged = employees.merge(departments, left_on='dept_id', right_on='id', how='outer')
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Full outer join
session.query(Employee.name, Department.name)
    .outerjoin(Department, Employee.dept_id == Department.id, full=True).all()

blocks.label: self join (manager lookup)
blocks.code:
-- Employee + their manager name
SELECT e.name AS employee, m.name AS manager
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id;
-- Same table, different aliases (e and m)
blocks.py-pandas:
# Self merge
merged = employees.merge(employees, left_on='manager_id', right_on='id', 
                         how='left', suffixes=('_emp', '_mgr'))
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Self join
m = aliased(Employee)
session.query(Employee.name, m.name.label('manager'))
    .outerjoin(m, Employee.manager_id == m.id).all()

items.q: FULL JOIN = LEFT JOIN UNION RIGHT JOIN? (ignoring duplicates)
items.explain: FULL JOIN = all left + all right. LEFT UNION RIGHT = same (UNION removes dups).
Aliases distinguish the two instances; FK to itself (manager_id → id) is the join condition.

blocks.label: union / intersect / except
blocks.code:
-- UNION: all distinct rows from both
SELECT name FROM employees
UNION
SELECT name FROM contractors;
-- Removes duplicates

-- UNION ALL: all rows, keep duplicates
SELECT name FROM employees
UNION ALL
SELECT name FROM contractors;
-- Faster, no dedup

-- INTERSECT: common rows
SELECT dept_id FROM employees
INTERSECT
SELECT id FROM departments;

-- EXCEPT: in first, not in second
SELECT dept_id FROM departments
EXCEPT
SELECT dept_id FROM employees;
-- Departments with NO employees
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL 8.0+: INTERSECT, EXCEPT supported
-- Older: use EXISTS/NOT EXISTS
blocks.py-pandas:
# Union
pd.concat([employees['name'], contractors['name']]).drop_duplicates()

# Union all
pd.concat([employees['name'], contractors['name']])

# Intersect
set(employees['dept_id']) & set(departments['id'])

# Except
set(departments['id']) - set(employees['dept_id'])
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Union
from sqlalchemy import union, union_all
q1 = session.query(Employee.name)
q2 = session.query(Contractor.name)
session.query(union(q1, q2)).all()

# Intersect/Except
from sqlalchemy import intersect, except_
session.query(intersect(...)).all()

items.explain: UNION ALL skips sort/unique. Use when duplicates OK or impossible.

items.q: EXCEPT is to NOT IN as INTERSECT is to:
items.explain: EXCEPT = in first not in second. INTERSECT = in both = IN logic.

revisionCard: INNER = intersection; LEFT = all left + match; RIGHT = all right + match; FULL = both
LEFT JOIN + WHERE right.id IS NULL = anti-join (left rows with no match)
JOIN condition in ON, not WHERE (especially for LEFT — WHERE filters after join)
Self join = table aliases + FK to same table (manager_id → id)
UNION = distinct (slow); UNION ALL = all rows (fast); use ALL when possible
INTERSECT = common; EXCEPT = in first not second

glossary.def: Returns only rows with matches in both tables (intersection).
All left rows; matched right rows or NULL (left circle + overlap).
All right rows; matched left rows or NULL (right circle + overlap).
All rows from both tables; NULLs where no match (union of circles).
Table joined to itself using aliases; FK references same table PK.
LEFT JOIN + WHERE right.key IS NULL — finds rows with no match.
